fr.elements: Main Residence; Access Drive; Circular Driveway; Open Lawn Area; Landscaped Area; Open Green Space
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Long Driveway; Open Terrain; Limited Rear Access
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the road entrance to the driveway so responders can identify the property quickly from the road.
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective posts on both sides to define its edges at night or in low-visibility conditions.
• Keep the circular driveway clear of parked vehicles so arriving apparatus can pull forward and turn without obstruction.
• Post the property address visibly at the driveway entrance, not only at the house, given the length of the drive.
• Identify and mark any secondary foot access point to the rear of the property so responders are not limited to the single vehicle access drive.
• Keep the lawn and open areas free of equipment, materials, or vehicles that would reduce available staging space for apparatus and crews.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Shrubs; Open Terrain; Scattered Trees; Brush Area; Vegetation Near Structure; Irrigated Landscape; Single Access Route; Long Driveway; Adequate Vegetation Separation; Grass Cover; Scattered Shrubs; Limited Rear Access
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim shrubs that are growing close to the house on any side where branches or stems touch or nearly touch the exterior.
• Thin scattered trees near the structure so their canopies do not overlap or connect with each other.
• Cut grass around the house and outbuildings regularly, especially during dry months when it dries out and lies flat.
• Remove or thin brush in the area behind the house where rear access is limited, to make that space easier to move through.
• Keep the long driveway clear of overhanging branches from edge trees and shrubs so vehicles can pass without obstruction.
• Trim back any shrubs or low branches that narrow the driveway or reduce visibility along its length.
• Mark the driveway entrance clearly so it is easy to locate when approaching from the main road.
• Move any wood piles, stored materials, or flammable objects away from the house and outbuildings.
• Keep irrigated landscaping beds directly next to the house free of dead leaves, dry mulch, and dry plant stems.
• Separate shrubs in the brush area from any nearby structures by removing plants closest to those structures first.
• Clear a walking path around the back of the house so the rear can be reached on foot without pushing through dense vegetation.
